name: Fixed Point Removal
description: Let $$$a_1, \ldots, a_n$$$ be an array of $$$n$$$ positive integers. In one operation, you can choose an index $$$i$$$ such that $$$a_i = i$$$, and remove $$$a_i$$$ from the array (after the removal, the remaining parts are concatenated). The weight of $$$a$$$ is defined as the maximum number of elements you can remove. You must answer $$$q$$$ independent queries $$$(x, y)$$$: after replacing the $$$x$$$ first elements of $$$a$$$ and the $$$y$$$ last elements of $$$a$$$ by $$$n+1$$$ (making them impossible to remove), what would be the weight of $$$a$$$?
input_specification: The first line contains two integers $$$n$$$ and $$$q$$$ ($$$1 \le n, q \le 3 \cdot 10^5$$$)  — the length of the array and the number of queries. The second line contains $$$n$$$ integers $$$a_1$$$, $$$a_2$$$, ..., $$$a_n$$$ ($$$1 \leq a_i \leq n$$$) — elements of the array. The $$$i$$$-th of the next $$$q$$$ lines contains two integers $$$x$$$ and $$$y$$$ ($$$x, y \ge 0$$$ and $$$x+y \lt n$$$).
output_specification: Print $$$q$$$ lines, $$$i$$$-th line should contain a single integer  — the answer to the $$$i$$$-th query.
approach_summary: Exploit monotonicity of two-pointer invariant [L, R]. Advance R while shifting L forward to maintain validity, running in O(N) amortized time.

topic_editorial.title: Editorial: 1404C — Fixed Point Removal [34. Two Pointers]
topic_editorial.key_invariant: When scanning contiguous subarrays or paired indices, advancing the right pointer $R$ monotonically tightens or relaxes the constraint, allowing the left pointer $L$ to only advance forward without ever needing to reset backwards.
